messages.subject: Function Q_spde
parts:
Dear TMB users.

I am a PhD student and I am using the package TMB.

I wonder if it is possible to use the function Q_spde in one dimension, using Lindgren et al (2011) notation, consider d = 1 and alpha = 1 or if it is only possible for d = 2 and alpha = 2?

In a R script I construct a mesh using function inla.mesh.1d and create the elements for sparse precision matrix using inla.spde2.matern (mesh, alpha=1). Then in a C++ file I want to use the function Q_spde but  I'm not sure if this is possible.

Best regards,
Andreia Monteiro

messages.author: 16c32bb3268768fd
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Function Q_spde
parts:
Hi Andreia,

I've posted a 1D GMRF model on my github (https://github.com/Andrea-Havron/gmrf_1D) for the situation where d=1, alpha = 1, nu = 0.5. This is a work in progress, so let me know if you run into any problems. 

Note that when d=1 and alpha = 1, nu = 0.5 and the Matern equals the Exponential covariance function {sigma2 * exp(-d/rho)}.  This being the case, you could also fit this type of data using an AR1 model with an exponential decay (see https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/classdensity_1_1AR1__t.html).

Best,
Andrea Havron
